blockNote: Player movement tick and collision helpers (184272-185206, Bank 02). PlayerMovementTick is the grounded-movement entry; the other routines are the shared helpers of the north / south / east / west handlers (player_move_ns, player_move_south, player_move_east, player_move_west).
=== ENTRY CONTRACT ===

PlayerMoveController (actors/player/player_move_controller) calls it with JSL once per frame when the player actor's flags word ($10) has bit $0008 set (grounded); airborne frames skip it and add the velocity to the position directly. X at entry is the CONTROLLER's own actor slot (the old note said the player actor): the tick saves it in the absolute scratch word $000A, and SetActorCollisionFlag later ORs bit $0004 (solid contact this tick) into that slot's $10; the controller copies the bit into the player's $10 when it writes the position back. The tick itself starts by clearing bit $0004 there.

D is set to $0000 for the whole tick, so the 2-digit operands below are low-RAM scratch words: $20 / $22 = X velocity / position, $24 / $26 = Y velocity / position, all in sub-pixels (4 per pixel, Y grows downward; the controller scaled the position by 4 before the call and wrote them to $22 / $26), $1A / $1E = the last probe's pixel X / Y, $00 / $02 / $04 = scratch, $AA / $AB = per-tick flag words (cleared together). The reference point of the 16x16 hitbox is the centre of its bottom edge.
=== TWO PHASES ===

1. Horizontal: the vertical velocity $24 is parked on the stack and zeroed. $20 = 0 skips the phase. Otherwise $AA bit $0040 is set (see below) and DispatchWestMove (negative $20) or DispatchEastMove (positive $20) runs. The old comments called this bit a 'diagonal flag'; it only records that the horizontal phase ran this tick. Afterwards $22 >> 2 and $26 >> 2 are stored in the player actor's pixel position ($0014 / $0016: the values are POSITIONS, not deltas as the old comments said) and $20 is cleared.

2. Vertical: the parked velocity is popped back into $24. Wall-slide handlers of the horizontal phase can zero the parked word (CancelVerticalPhase in player_move_west), which then cancels this phase. Zero skips it, negative runs DispatchNorthMove, positive runs DispatchSouthMove. The controller commits the final $22 / $26 after the tick returns.

$AA bits: $0040 = horizontal phase ran (read by AutoAlignEW here and AutoAlignEW_South, which refuse to nudge in that case). $0800 and $0400 are tested before the north and south dispatch (the old comments called them 'south wall' and 'east wall' contact), but nothing in extracted/ ever sets them; player_move_west only clears them (TRB #$0840 / #$0440). Those two gates therefore always pass (OQ-I045-1). $AB bit 1 is set by DispatchWestMove and read by player_move_ns.
=== AutoAlignEW (north counterpart of AutoAlignEW_South) ===

Called only from the blocked path of DispatchNorthMove. Returns carry CLEAR when X was nudged by 2 pixels toward the open column, carry SET when nothing was done. Gates (carry set): $AA bit $0040, an actor solid mark in the collision byte at the map index left in X by the last probe (high nibble), or n = 0. n = (($22 >> 2) - 8) AND $0F is the offset of the hitbox's LEFT edge (X - 8) inside its 16-pixel column. n >= 6 tries an east nudge first: it needs ProbeFutureTR to return a type below $0E and not $06. If that fails (or n < 6) and n < 9, a west nudge is tried: ProbeFutureTL below $0E and not $09. So n = 1..5 can only go west, 6..8 prefers east, 9..15 can only go east. The old text gave the east range as '6-8' and the west range as 'offset 1-8, via 9+ check'.

Each nudge temporarily subtracts $20 sub-pixels (8 px) from $22 so that the helper tests the left edge, calls NudgeToLowerGrid (+8) or NudgeToUpperGrid (-8), then adds $20 back; the 2-pixel nudge itself stays in $22.
=== NUDGE HELPERS ===

Both work on the word at [$00 + X] (X = $22 for the X position, X = $26 for the Y position in player_move_east / player_move_west). NudgeToLowerGrid adds 8 sub-pixels (toward larger coordinates: east or south); if that crosses a $40 line (16 px) the result is floored to the line (AND #$FFC0), so the edge ends exactly flush. NudgeToUpperGrid subtracts 8 and, on crossing a $40 line, clamps back up to that line ((value AND #$FFC0) + $40). The 'lower' and 'upper' in the names refer to coordinate order, not to a screen direction.
=== ComputeYSnapOffset ===

$02 = 16 - (probe pixel Y AND $0F): the number of pixels to the next row line below, 1..16 ($10 when the probe is already flush). The old header said an aligned probe gives $0000; the code (OR #$FFF0, EOR #$FFFF, INC) gives $10. $1E is a pixel Y, not a sub-pixel position. Called from player_move_ns only (2 sites).
=== DiagSnapCompute_Unused ===

No reference anywhere in extracted/. It probes the current TL cell and takes the 'wall path' when the type is $06, or when X straddles two columns and the cell to the right is $09 (the same wall-like types as the north handlers; the old text called $06 a 'slope / transition' type and mentioned a DispatchDiag* system that does not exist). On the wall path $02 starts at 0; a nonzero $24 is converted to a pixel step ((>>2) OR #$C000 sign-extends only a NEGATIVE value, so it assumes a north move), negated, added to the saved Y, and if that crosses a 16-px line ($1E bit 4 changes) $02 = $10. The ComputeYSnapOffset formula for the current $1E is then added to $02. The probe coordinates $1A / $1E are saved and restored around the probe.
Everything here is UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (no emulator trace); the arithmetic is read from the code.

PlayerMovementTick: Per-frame grounded movement, called by PlayerMoveController. Parks $24, runs the horizontal phase (West / East dispatch), publishes the horizontal result to the player actor's pixel position, un-parks $24 and runs the vertical phase (North / South dispatch). X = controller slot at entry; D = $0000 inside; P, D and X are restored.

blockNote: Orbit placement helper (Bank 00, 62409-62503). It sets the calling actor's position to a base point plus a circular offset: X += sin(angle) * r, Y += cos(angle) * r with r = diameter / 2. Two entries:
- ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef: Y = a reference actor (slot address). Copies that actor's pixel X / Y ($0014 / $0016) into the caller's $14 / $16 first, then falls into the second entry.

- code_00F3D3: skips the copy and ADDS the offset to whatever $14 / $16 already hold, so the caller must have written the centre there (otherwise the offset accumulates). It is entered from 5 sites (mtA1_fire_sprite 2, attack_ability_system, pyDD_queen_spirit_attack, unused_mode7_boss).

Inputs: X = the caller's actor slot, D = X (the DP $14 / $16 are the caller's), 16-bit A. orbitAngle ($7F0010,X) is read as a BYTE: 256 steps per turn, 1.40625 degrees each. orbitDiameter ($7F0012,X) is also read as a byte, so a diameter above 255 is not possible. The routine clobbers A, Y and the flags, keeps X and D, and returns with A 16-bit.

Arithmetic: for each axis the table value (sine_table_8bit for X, signed_cosine_table_8bit for Y, both indexed by the angle byte; the sine table is only a quarter wave and entries 64-255 read on into the cosine table) is turned into a magnitude, the sign is kept in the carry flag, the magnitude times the diameter is formed with Multiply8x8Unsigned (which preserves carry and Y), the high byte of the 16-bit product is taken (>> 8) and negated when the carry says so. The table peak is $7F, so each offset is about +/- diameter / 2 (the name 'diameter' is right: it is the full width of the circle). Angle 0 puts the actor directly BELOW the centre (cosine peak, Y grows downward); $40 is east, $80 north, $C0 west, so increasing angles turn counter-clockwise on screen.

Callers: 21 JSL sites in 11 files: attack_ability_system 2, btE4_kara, ec0E_lily, ir29_castoth, mtA1_fire_sprite 5, pyDD_queen_orb_shot, pyDD_queen_spirit_attack, cop_handlers_effects (SpiralStep, with the reference actor in $0000), item_use_system, statue_inventory_reward and unused_mode7_boss 6. 16 use the first entry and 5 the second. The elliptical variant with separate X / Y angles is ApplyOrbitalOffsetXY.

The old header said 'multiplied by orbitDiameter ... result updates actor $14/$16' without the sign, byte-width and rotation direction facts above. UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (read from the code and the table headers).

loc_00F40D: Y axis: multiply the cosine magnitude by the diameter (carry = sign), keep the high byte, negate if needed.

blockNote: Particle rain spawner (Bank 0B, 774827-774918): a looping actor that spawns falling particle children at an increasing rate, plus the child (ParticleRainChild). It is NOT used: no spawn table, script or thinker references particle_rain_spawner anywhere in extracted/ (the old header said 'used for the ending credits particle rain'; docs/code/bank0B... lists it as unreferenced). actor-def <#00,#00,#38>.
=== SPAWNER ===

$24 starts at $78. Each cycle: if $24 is not 4, decrement it; store $24 in the wait counter $08; SetEntryHereAndYield; spawn a child. The wait counter resumes the actor after N + 1 ticks (see WaitByte), so the intervals are 120, 119, 118 ... 5 ticks and then 5 ticks forever (the old note said the delay shrinks to 4 frames; the real minimum is 5). The spawn rate therefore RISES with time: the old part note called this 'decelerating'; only the delay decelerates. The ramp takes 7,250 ticks (about 2 minutes) to reach the steady rate. UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME.
COP SpawnAfterFlags ( @ParticleRainChild, #$1802 ) writes $1802 into the child's flags word $10; CopyActorState copies the spawner's position, anim index and pointers.
=== CHILD ===

SetMetasprite points the child at spriteset_enemies and StageSprAndHitbox #02 shows animation list 2 (sprite_set_0EE0A6: 7 frames, hold 2 each, so one pass is 21 ticks). Priority operand $30 sets OAM priority bits $3000 (frontmost). Start: Y = $FFE0 (-32), X = RNG * 2 + $C4, i.e. $C4-$2C2 in steps of 2. The same random byte also picks the speed: index = (RNG AND 3) * 2 + 4.

The values stored in moveXAlt / moveYAlt are MOVEMENT INDICES into movement_delta_table, not velocities (the old comments said 'X velocity 4, 6, 8, 10 / Y velocity 3, 5, 7, 9'). Odd indices are +n, even indices are -n pixels per frame (index 3 = +2, 4 = -2, 5 = +3, 6 = -3 ...). The child therefore moves X by -2, -3, -4 or -5 and Y by +2, +3, +4 or +5 per frame (index X = 4/6/8/10 pairs with Y = 3/5/7/9, equal magnitudes): it falls DIAGONALLY down and to the left at 45 degrees, not straight down.

ReloadMoveDurations re-arms the two delta chains; AnimOnce zeroes $2C / $2E when its list ends, which is why the loop reloads them after every pass. The death test (Y >= $0200, unsigned) runs only when an animation pass has ended, i.e. every 21 ticks, not every frame. A particle whose Y were still negative at that moment would be read as a huge unsigned value and die; at 21 ticks the slowest particle (+2 per frame from -32) is at +10, so by the numbers all of them survive the first check (UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME, OQ-I045-2).
docs/code/bank0B-late-bosses-system-cutscene-actors.md also says the particles 'rise via ReloadForceMove' from 'screen top'; they start above the screen and FALL.
